content_screening.policy: Exclude reported/inherently sensitive headwords even when they have neutral senses. Screen every English gloss before definition selection, including whole-word inflections and recognized compounds. Filter killing/murder mentions in any context, weapon mentions, toilet language, demeaning terms, alcohol/tobacco, graphic and sexual content. Other ordinary words may keep suitable independent senses.
content_screening.punjabi: Explicit native/roman headword bans remove paired source records; English vocabulary matching applies to English glosses, never indiscriminately to Roman Punjabi lookup spellings.
content_screening.limitation: Conservative reproducible screening, not exhaustive human editorial review. A filtered sense is not rewritten or restored.

rules: Unique lowercase ASCII headwords of exactly the requested length; alphabetical order.
No spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, digits, or capitalized source lemmas (including capitalized names and acronyms).
Headword blocklist plus conservative screening of definitions for profanity, slurs, adult/explicit material, and graphic subjects.
Shared v2 content rules also exclude killing/murder, weapons, toilet language, demeaning word families, alcohol/tobacco, and reported sensitive headwords even when a neutral sense exists.
Safe senses of otherwise acceptable words are retained; unsafe senses and usage examples are omitted.

Include lowercase WordNet headwords and explicitly recorded 4-6-letter exception-table inflections absent as lexical headwords; do not invent regular inflections. Existing headword senses remain authoritative.

Inflections inherit only suitable same-POS base senses with original definition wording, base_word, and exception-file provenance. Screen both base and surface words; bases may be outside the 4-6 range.
metadata.limitation: Automated filtering with targeted editorial screening, not a complete human review or a certification of child suitability. Rare and technical vocabulary remains. WordNet emphasizes nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs rather than every English word.

definition_selection.name: Most frequently tagged suitable WordNet sense with a clarity preference
definition_selection.source: WordNet-3.0/dict/index.sense in the original downloaded archive
ranking: Prefer descriptive wording over generic standalone definitions such as 'have' or 'engage in', or fragments ending with a comma/colon, when an alternative exists.
Highest word-specific tagged usage count among the already-filtered definitions, comparing all available parts of speech.
If tied (including all-zero counts), lowest WordNet sense number within its part of speech.
If still tied, original order: noun, verb, adjective, adverb.
definition_selection.inflections: Exception-table forms use the source base word's same-POS senses, tagged counts, and sense numbers; these are not observed counts for the inflected spelling. The selected entry identifies base_word and tag_count_basis.
definition_selection.limitation: Tag counts come from WordNet's historical semantically tagged texts and are not current population-wide usage frequencies. Many rare words have no tagged occurrences. Selection is a reproducible heuristic, not a human judgment of the best game clue.

metadata.packaging: Combined length groups; added explicit tile_count and English letter_units; original wording and source sense fields preserved.
